result_semantic_payload.summary:
YES — the device contains direct, content-level evidence of a scripted, persona-based investment-fraud operation. Five plaintext files were recovered (all 5 files in the file index, none deleted, all at the same mtime 1789924915 and created at 1789924922, inodes 12/14/15/17/18 — contiguous, indicating a single batch write):

(1) 话术/开场白.txt — an outbound cold-contact script using a fabricated persona: "您好,我是金玉财经的首席分析师助理…历史年化收益超过30%…老师每天盘中实时带单,名额有限,先到先得。请添加老师微信,领取新手体验金888元。" (fabricated analyst-assistant identity, inflated historical return claim, scarcity pressure, WeChat off-platform migration, bait incentive).

(2) 话术/应对拒绝.txt — objection-handling rebuttals: "客户说考虑一下:老师今天带单已经盈利12%,机会稍纵即逝。客户质疑资质:我们平台受境外监管,出入金秒到账,可以小额试水。" (urgency framing, unverifiable "overseas-regulated" claim, low-barrier "test deposit" tactic — classic 杀猪盘 pattern).

(3) README.md — "内部资料,严禁外传 / 平台名称:金玉满堂 / 管理后台: 172.16.8.66:9090" (confidentiality marking plus a named platform and an internal admin endpoint).

(4) data/客户清单.csv — 3 victims/targets with name, phone, invested amount, status: 王芳 13812345678 50000 已入金; 李强 13987654321 120000 追单中; 赵敏 13666688888 8000 观望.

(5) data/入金记录.txt — 2 deposit records: "2022-06-19 王芳 USDT转账 50000元 卡号6222020200112233445 张某某" and "2022-06-21 李强 USDT转账 120000元 钱包0xFAKE1234567890ABCDEF".

Cross-file internal consistency is strong: 王芳 50,000 and 李强 120,000 appear identically in both the client list and the deposit log; the victim set in the deposit log is a subset of the client list.

WHAT CAN BE CONCLUDED: (a) scripted, persona-based fraud materials exist on the device, including a fabricated persona and a two-stage rebuttal playbook; (b) a named platform ("金玉满堂"/"金玉财经") and an internal admin host 172.16.8.66:9090 are referenced; (c) three named targets with phone numbers and investment amounts are tracked with pipeline statuses (已入金/追单中/观望); (d) two USDT-based deposits totalling 170,000 元 are recorded against two of those targets, dated 2022-06-19 and 2022-06-21; (e) the files were written in one contiguous batch.

WHAT CANNOT BE CONCLUDED (see limitations): no evidence that any call/message was actually delivered, that victims were actually contacted or defrauded, that the USDT transfers settled, or that the "platform" is real; no attribution of authorship or operator identity to any individual; no malware, no live network activity, no account/execution traces corroborating use of the scripts; the deposit log is self-reported plaintext with no independent ledger corroboration; the evidence cannot distinguish an active operation from a template, training set, or sample material.

The only export recorded in /export/app.log on 2024-05-10 was performed by the account 'svc_export' (EXPORT account=svc_export dataset=customers rows=184112 dest=/backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz at 01:03:22, status=success at 01:03:40, duration 18s). That export was preceded at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 by 'SCHEDULE job=nightly_export account=svc_export triggered', matching the daily 23:55 schedule defined in /scheduler/jobs.conf. /README.txt explicitly describes svc_export as a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs. The only lihua activity in the log is two FAILED login attempts at 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from 198.51.100.44 (reason=password) — i.e., lihua never authenticated successfully, and those attempts occurred ~43 minutes AFTER the export completed. Attribution: the export was performed by the automated nightly_export job running as the service account svc_export.

claim_candidates.text: On 2024-05-10 the customer-dataset export recorded in /export/app.log was performed by account 'svc_export', not by lihua; the log line at 01:03:22 attributes EXPORT dataset=customers rows=184112 dest=/backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz to account=svc_export and the 01:03:40 status=success line is also attributed to svc_export.

The export was triggered by the scheduled job 'nightly_export' at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 (SCHEDULE job=nightly_export account=svc_export triggered), which matches the daily 23:55 schedule defined in /scheduler/jobs.conf.
svc_export is a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs, per the case README on the seized application server.

lihua produced no successful authentication and no export action in the recorded evidence; the only lihua entries are two FAILED login attempts at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from 198.51.100.44 (reason=password).

The lihua failed-login attempts occurred ~43 minutes after the export completed (export finished 01:03:40; lihua attempts 01:47:11/01:47:59), so lihua could not have been the actor for that export based on the recorded log ordering.
The analyst's hypothesis that lihua exported the customer database on 2024-05-10 is refuted by the available evidence; the actor was the automated nightly_export job running as svc_export.

The two lihua failed logins from 198.51.100.44 shortly after the export warrant a separate investigation (possible credential guessing / lateral-movement attempt against the account of an employee the analyst suspected), but this is not corroborated by the current evidence.

limitations: Only three files are available (/export/app.log, /scheduler/jobs.conf, /README.txt); no authentication logs, no Windows event logs, no registry/prefetch/amcache, and no network captures are present, so corroboration beyond the single app.log is impossible.

The export destination /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz is referenced in the log but the artifact itself is not present in the image; its existence, integrity and transfer path are unverified.

All three files share the same mtime/ctime (1790594134), so file-level timestamps do not independently corroborate the 2024-05-10 log timeline; the log's internal timestamps are the sole temporal basis.

The lihua failed logins from 198.51.100.44 shortly after the export are a plausible but uncorroborated lead and should be investigated separately rather than assumed innocent.

result_semantic_payload.summary: The device (a seized workstation) holds a small but coherent evidentiary footprint of a payment-collection operation, concentrated in two directories: /data/收款记录.txt (a three-row cash-in ledger) and /platform/说明.txt (platform operator notes). Together they show a recurring USDT-based collection ledger naming three payers (陈某, 周某, 吴某), two recipient instruments (one bank card number and one wallet address that is reused across two entries), and an internal platform named "聚宝盆" with an admin URL and a per-agent daily new-user recruitment quota of 20 — the last being the operational-mechanism indicator that most plausibly explains why funds are being collected. /personal/体检报告.txt is a medical check-up report belonging to 陈某 (one of the three payers) that is expressly unrelated to any fund activity and must be kept out of the evidentiary chain, as the on-device README.txt itself directs. Two important scope caveats: the task metadata declares no platform scenario and no registered source scopes, so no Windows-native sources (prefetch, Amcache, registry, Event Logs, browser/app telemetry, file-system metadata beyond creation timestamps) were available — the four plain-text dumps are the entire captured corpus. All four files share a single synthetic creation timestamp (epoch 1790594136) and carry empty MD5 fields, so no independent integrity or sequencing corroboration exists. The payment ledger and the platform notes are therefore content-evidence only; they are not corroborated by any execution trace, and the README.txt is a meta/annotation file describing the collection layout rather than a transaction record.

claim_candidates.text: The device holds a payment-collection ledger at /data/收款记录.txt recording three USDT cash-ins: 2023-11-02 陈某 USDT 30000 to bank card 6222020212345678901; 2023-11-04 周某 USDT 17500 to wallet 0xDEAD1111; 2023-11-09 吴某 USDT 52000 to wallet 0xDEAD1111 (aggregate 99,500 USDT).

Wallet address 0xDEAD1111 is the collection instrument for two of the three entries (周某 and 吴某), and the bank card 6222020212345678901 is the instrument for the 陈某 entry, indicating a single operator-controlled collection channel.

The device holds platform operator notes at /platform/说明.txt naming an internal platform '聚宝盆', an admin address http://jbpenl-admin.example, and a per-customer-service-group daily new-user recruitment quota of 20 people.

The daily-20 new-user recruitment quota, read together with the USDT cash-in ledger, indicates a recruitment-driven collection operation: users are acquired on a quota basis and then pay into the operator's collection instruments.

/personal/体检报告.txt (a 2023-10-20 medical check-up report for 陈某 stating blood pressure normal, elevated blood lipids, re-check advised, and explicitly 'unrelated to any fund activity') must be excluded from the evidentiary chain supporting the payment-collection operation.

The on-device README.txt itself instructs that the personal directory holds the owner's private documents with no evidential relation to the payment operation and that they must not be cited as evidence of it.
Payer 陈某 appears in both the payment ledger and the excluded medical report; the name overlap is a data linkage only and does not make the medical report evidentiary.

No execution or user-activity corroboration exists for these documents: the only timeline events are four FILE_CREATED records at a single identical timestamp, with no prefetch, Amcache, registry, event-log, or browser telemetry available in this scope.

limitations: Task metadata exposes no platform scenario and no registered source scopes, so no Windows-native sources (prefetch, Amcache, registry, Event Logs, browser/app telemetry) were available; the four plain-text dumps are the entire captured corpus.
All four files share a single identical creation timestamp (epoch 1790594136) and empty MD5 fields, so no independent integrity, authorship, or sequencing corroboration exists.
Payment ledger amounts are self-reported text entries with no on-chain or banking confirmation; the payer names are unverified aliases (陈某/周某/吴某).
The link between the platform '聚宝盆' and the recorded USDT cash-ins is an inference from co-location and content, not a demonstrated transactional connection.
The exclusion ruling for /personal/体检报告.txt rests on the document's own content plus the on-device README.txt instruction; it is a scope/relevance determination, not a legal privilege ruling.
/README.txt is treated as a meta-annotation file, not as an independent transaction record.
